messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 - abnormal CUDA illegal memory access rate detected on prod-gpu-pool-us-west-2. Error: \"CUDA illegal memory access (misaligned address)\" observed across multiple containers. Auto-alerting from 1993456700 UTC.

sam (on-call-sre): I see node flaps and a small spike in OOM-related restarts. Rolling metrics: 8 nodes showing restart loops, ~12% request errors for the text-gen route. Correlation with paging activity on those nodes.

lee (on-call-ml): Confirmed. Logs show repeated kernel warnings then CUDA illegal memory access in runtime lib. Possibly a race during KV cache eviction when page-in occurs. Happening mostly for long context requests (>8k tokens).

carol (eng-runtime): Pasted the most relevant snippet from one of the failing containers:
```
2026-11-03T14:12:34Z runtime ERROR: CUDA error: Illegal memory access at 0x7ffb3c12
stack: server.cpp:492 handle_step -> attention_kernels.cu:211 __global__ -> memcpy_async -> cudaErrorIllegalAddress
container restart triggered by OOM killer shortly after.
```

mike (prod-support): Customer impact: 3 customers reported elevated 500s for chat-api in the last 20m, one is in-flight enterprise customer on Dedicated. CS is already triaging with the customer (julia).

julia (customer-success): I've opened a bridge with the customer and told them we're investigating. They're seeing request failures and token truncation. They've accepted temporary latency increases but want ETA for mitigation.

sam (on-call-sre): Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Drain the 8 affected nodes from prod-gpu-pool-us-west-2 to stop further noisy restarts. 2) Scale up spare nodes in the pool (warm nodes) and fail traffic to them. 3) Apply emergency runtime config: disable long-prefix batching + reduce max_context to 4096 for the routed model variant. 4) Notify customers about degraded capacity.

carol (eng-runtime): Agree with plan. I'm preparing a hotpatch to tighten KV cache eviction ordering and add bounds checks. Hotpatch will be staged to dedicated canary first. If we can keep the canary stable for 5 minutes, we can roll to the rest.

ops-runbooks: Runbook checklist applied: https://internal/runbooks/illegal-memory-access - steps executed: drain nodes, preserve /var/log/containers, snapshot dmesg, mark nodes unschedulable.

lee (on-call-ml): Quick test: pushing a fallback route that points to smaller quantized model (gpt-small-q4) for affected customers/keys. This should reduce memory pressure and avoid long-kernel paths. Doing canary with 5% traffic now.

incident-bot: Canary rollout started at 1993456870, 5% traffic -> gpt-small-q4. Monitoring errors.

mike (prod-support): Error rate on the main route dropped from 12% -> 4% after canary redirect started. Still seeing container restart loops on drained nodes (expected until reboot).

sam (on-call-sre): Reboots in progress. We're collecting kernel oops and nvcc stack traces. Also enabling memory compaction with echo 1 > /proc/sys/vm/compact_memory on remaining nodes as precaution.

carol (eng-runtime): Hotpatch prepared, small guard inserted into attention kernel caller to handle misaligned pointer during concurrent eviction. Patch size is tiny; compiling with CI now. If CI passes within 6m I'll push to canary.

lee (on-call-ml): Observed that requests that trigger page-in from cold KV cache are most likely to hit the bug. As longer contexts warm the KV cache, chance of misalignment increases when eviction runs concurrently. Hypothesis: a race between eviction and page-in on host memory mapping.

julia (customer-success): Relay to customer: we have a mitigation rolling (fallback model + node drainage) and a patch in CI. ETA for full resolution ~2-3 hours depending on patch validation. Customer acknowledged.

sam (on-call-sre): Handoff: I'm on-call until 16:00 UTC. After that, lee will be primary for runtime verification. Leaving a short list of follow-ups in the incident ticket: collect crash dumps, capture unrolled kernel traces, and collaborate with infra to check NIC firmware logs.

lee (on-call-ml): Taking over at 16:00 UTC. Will coordinate patch canary and rollback thresholds. Proposed rollback if error rate >1% for >5 minutes on canary.

carol (eng-runtime): CI green. Pushing hotpatch to canary (g-prod-canary-3). Patch includes: extra bounds check, serialized eviction step for KV cache during async page-in, and additional debug logging controlled by runtime flag. Will keep flag off in prod to avoid perf hit unless we need more traces.

incident-bot: Hotpatch deployed to canary at 1993456985. 1% of traffic. Observability hooks enabled: token-level latency, cuda_error_count, container_restart_count.

mike (prod-support): After canary deploy, canary error_count -> 0 for 12 minutes. No restarts observed on canary nodes. Main pool error rate continuing downward after draining affected nodes.

sam (on-call-sre): Summary log for postmortem: timeline, nodes drained (list in ticket), canary results, customer impact (3 customers, degraded for ~25m, two temporary throttles applied), proposed RCAs and next steps.

carol (eng-runtime): Next steps: 1) Plan a full rollback-safe rollout of hotpatch with staged percentages (10/30/60). 2) Add regression test simulating concurrent eviction + page-in on long-context requests. 3) Add built-in runtime metric to detect misaligned pointer condition early. 4) Consider kernel param tweaks or driver update if hardware-level misalignment appears.

lee (on-call-ml): I'll keep monitoring for 2 hours post-rollout and validate we see no recurrence at scale. If stable, we'll mark incident resolved and schedule postmortem.

julia (customer-success): Customers updated; two requested notes for postmortem. They want to know root cause and what prevents recurrence.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial; active mitigations in place, patch canary success. Full rollout pending staged validation.

sam (on-call-sre): Leaving the channel for handoff, tagging the ticket "severities/SEV-2". Handing to lee. :white_check_mark:

lee (on-call-ml): Acknowledged. I have control of the rollout and will update this thread with final outcome and postmortem link.

carol (eng-runtime): Noting that we'll include the failing stack traces and the micro-repro in the postmortem. Thanks everyone for quick coordination.

mike (prod-support): Closing customer-facing notes after final rollout.

(reacts: incident-bot :eyes:, sam :thumbsup:, carol :rocket:)
